summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an undeclared obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs (using obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNN` identifiers) downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts and chmods the `bun` binary, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a sibling file `math_init.js` inside the package. `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle carrying a shuffled string-constants array, a rotate-shift decoder, and hex-obfuscated identifiers — no readable source is shipped. This file is not declared in package.json's `files` array (which lists only `bin/` and `README.md`), yet ships in the tarball. The advertised purpose is a minimal-dependency Rust coding agent, and `bin/cli-main.js` explicitly claims 'zero install-time cost beyond node itself', which contradicts the actual preinstall behavior. The combination of alternate-runtime execution at install time, heavy obfuscation of the executed payload, and omission of the payload from the declared publish surface matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: a downloaded second runtime executes obfuscated bundled code on the installer's machine during `npm install`, evading Node-based inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
